Let $x$ be an n-dimensional vector. Let $u$ be an m-dimensional vector. Let $A$ be an n by n matrix. Let $B$ be an n by m matrix. The continuous-time state equation is $\dot{x}=Ax+Bu$.

Let $y$ be a p-dimensional vector. Let $x$ be an n-dimensional vector. Let $u$ be an m-dimensional vector. Let $C$ be a p by n matrix. Let $D$ be a p by m matrix. A state-space output equation is \[y=Cx+Du\].
The transfer function is $G(s)=Y(s)/U(s)$.
The state-space transfer matrix is \[G(s)=C(sI-A)^{-1}B+D.\]
Let $u$ be an m-dimensional vector. Let $K$ be an m by n matrix. Let $x$ be an n-dimensional vector. Let $r$ be an m-dimensional vector. Negative state feedback uses $u=-Kx+r$.
Let $A$ be an n by n matrix. Let $B$ be an n by m matrix. Let $K$ be an m by n matrix. The closed-loop state matrix is \[A_{cl}=A-BK\].
Closed-loop poles satisfy $\det(sI-A)=0$.
Let $A$, $P$, and $Q$ be n by n matrices. A continuous Lyapunov equation is \[A^TP+PA=-Q\].
Let $A$, $P$, and $Q$ be n by n matrices. A discrete Lyapunov equation is $A^TPA-P=-Q$.
The controllability matrix is \[\mathcal{C}=[B\ AB\ \cdots\ A^{n-1}B].\]
The observability matrix is $\mathcal{O}=[C^T,(CA)^T,\ldots]^T$.
The reachability Gramian is \[W_c=\int_0^\infty e^{At}BB^Te^{A^Tt}dt.\]
The observability Gramian is $W_o=\int_0^\infty e^{A^Tt}C^TCe^{At}dt$.
A PID controller has \[u=K_pe+K_i\int e\,dt+K_d\dot e.\]
The finite-horizon quadratic cost is $J=\int_0^T(x^TQx+u^TRu)dt$.
The algebraic Riccati equation is \[A^TP+PA-PBR^{-1}B^TP+Q=0.\]
A Kalman prediction step is $\hat{x}_{k|k-1}=A\hat{x}_{k-1|k-1}$.
The estimator update is \[\hat{x}_{k|k}=\hat{x}_{k|k-1}+K_k(y_k-C\hat{x}_{k|k-1}).\]
A discrete transfer matrix is $G(z)=C(zI-A)^{-1}B+D$.
Frequency response is evaluated as \[G(j\omega).\]
